original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Income and Outlays release published 2026-08-26. Resolve TRUE if the published July 2026 core PCE price index month-over-month percentage change is 0.3% or higher at the precision reported in the release; otherwise resolve FALSE. Score the 0.36 binary probability by Brier score and log loss. Score the 0.2% point estimate by absolute error against the same first-release value, compare it with the frozen 0.1% no-change, 0.2% published-consensus, and 0.3% Trading Economics model point benchmarks, and record whether the first-release value falls inside the 0.1%-0.4% 80% interval. Do not substitute later revisions unless BEA corrects the initial release before scoring.
rationale: H001 and H003 are tied at 0.34 after the Aug. 24 model update, making underlying core-inflation persistence a high-information discriminator.

The frozen published consensus is 0.2% m/m while Trading Economics' model forecast is 0.3%, providing an external disagreement around the threshold rather than a threshold chosen solely for scoring convenience.

Recent strong services activity and still-elevated price pressure preserve upside risk, but Monday's oil/yield relief and July household weakness prevent an above-consensus probability greater than 0.5.

July core PCE substantially predates the late-August oil escalation. This forecast is explicitly a test of underlying core inflation persistence and must not be scored or interpreted as a test of the August oil-pass-through hypothesis.
surprising_if: Core PCE is >=0.4% m/m, indicating materially stronger underlying core persistence than the model assigns high probability.
Core PCE is <=0.0% m/m while contemporaneous activity remains strong, which would sharply favor the benign-disinflation branch over H003's core-persistence branch.

resolution.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, first Personal Income and Outlays release for July 2026, published 2026-08-26 at 08:30 EDT: PCE price index excluding food and energy increased 0.2% from June and 3.3% from a year earlier.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved without hindsight alteration. The >=0.3% event resolved FALSE at the published 0.2%. The 0.36 probability earned a better Brier score than the neutral 0.50 comparator. The 0.2% point estimate was exact, but it exactly matched the frozen published consensus, so the zero point error is not evidence of information beyond consensus. The 80% interval covered. This resolution tests July underlying core persistence only; it does not test later-August oil pass-through.
